goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/post.rb:131 — `cook` returns `raw` verbatim when `cook_method == :raw_html`, so imported feed content is stored and rendered unsanitized, producing stored XSS on the main forum

adjudication.rationale:
The diff explicitly adds a new `cook_method` and changes `Post#cook` to `return raw` when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, bypassing the normal cooking/rendering pipeline (which is where Discourse typically sanitizes/filters HTML). New code paths create posts with `cook_method: :raw_html` from untrusted remote content:
- `Jobs::PollFeed` pulls `i.content` from a remote feed (`open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)`), unescapes HTML, and passes it to `TopicEmbed.import` with no sanitization.
- `TopicEmbed.import` writes that content into a post (`PostCreator.new(... raw: absolutize_urls(url, contents), ... cook_method: :raw_html)`), and `absolutize_urls` only rewrites relative `href`/`src` but does not strip dangerous tags/attributes.
Since these are normal posts in the forum, returning/storing and later rendering the raw HTML as cooked content makes stored XSS plausible and directly introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:4 — adding `force: true` to an already-shipped `create_table` migration silently DROPs the existing `top_topics` table and its data on re-run; same issue in 20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:3

adjudication.rationale: `create_table ..., force: true` will indeed drop an existing table before creating it *if that migration is executed while the table already exists*. However, the diff changes an already-versioned migration (`20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb`), and Rails will not re-run it on existing installations where it has already been applied (it’s tracked in `schema_migrations`). So this change does not introduce a verifiable data-loss path in normal upgrade/migrate flows. The new `create_topic_embeds` migration is being introduced for the first time, so there is no existing `topic_embeds` table/data to “silently drop” under normal execution either. The finding hinges on atypical scenarios (manually re-running an old migration against an existing table), which is not a clear defect evidenced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:26-27 — framing control uses `X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL`, which is not a valid XFO value and is ignored by browsers, so no framing restriction is applied

app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:26-27 — access control compares only `URI(request.referer).host` to `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`; Referer is spoofable/omittable and host-only comparison ignores scheme and port

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, access is gated by `URI(request.referer || '').host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host`. This relies on the HTTP Referer header, which is client-controlled/spoofable in non-browser contexts and can be omitted/modified by user agents (the code already rejects missing referer, but that doesn’t make it trustworthy). Also, the comparison uses only `host`, ignoring scheme and port, so a referer from the same host on a different port (or scheme) would pass even if that distinction matters for the embedding trust boundary.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:12 — `contents << "\n<hr>..."` mutates the caller's string in place, causing duplicate footers on repeated use and RuntimeError on frozen strings

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicEmbed.import`, `contents << "\n<hr>..."` appends to the `contents` object in place. That is a verifiable side effect: any caller holding a reference to the same String will see it modified (so reusing the same String for multiple imports would accumulate multiple footers). Additionally, if a caller passes a frozen String (possible via `"...".freeze` or other sources), this line will raise at runtime (FrozenError/RuntimeError depending on Ruby version). The mutation is introduced directly by this diff and is not mitigated elsewhere in the method.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:16 — origin check `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` accepts any origin that is a substring of the configured URL instead of requiring an exact origin match
app/models/topic_embed.rb:12 — feed item URL interpolated unescaped into `#{url}`, allowing markup/attribute injection into the stored post

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicEmbed.import`, the code appends `"#{url}"` into `contents` without any escaping. The only guard is `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which merely checks the prefix and still allows quotes/whitespace (e.g. `http://example.com' onmouseover='...`). Because imported posts are created with `cook_method: :raw_html` and later rendered via `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, this unescaped interpolation can lead to stored markup/attribute injection in the embedded view.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:15-30 — check-then-create TOCTOU race on `embed_url` with a unique index between RetrieveTopic, PollFeed, and concurrent requests, causing ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique and duplicate topics; TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve `exists?` guard has the same gap

adjudication.rationale: Yes. `TopicEmbed.import` does a non-atomic check-then-create: it queries `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and if blank proceeds to create a post/topic and then `TopicEmbed.create!` for the same `embed_url`. Since there is a unique index on `topic_embeds.embed_url`, concurrent callers (e.g., multiple `RetrieveTopic` jobs, `PollFeed`, or concurrent embed requests) can both observe no row and race to insert, causing `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` on the losing transaction. `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` has the same TOCTOU gap via `exists?` followed by later creation. The “duplicate topics” part is less certain because the create is wrapped in a transaction that should roll back on the uniqueness exception, but the unhandled `RecordNotUnique` failure under concurrency is a real, diff-verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:41-43 — `perform_retrieve` calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` synchronously, causing a full feed download and import of every item inline per embed miss

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In lib/topic_retriever.rb#perform_retrieve, when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true it directly calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` (synchronous, not enqueued). `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` then does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and iterates `rss.items.each` importing every item via `TopicEmbed.import`. This means a single embed miss can trigger a full feed download and full-item import inline within the retriever’s execution path (and since the throttle key is per-embed URL, different misses can cause repeated full feed polls).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/embed/loading.html.erb:8-10 — the loading page reloads unconditionally every 30s forever with no attempt cap or backoff, re-enqueueing RetrieveTopic indefinitely when retrieval permanently fails

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#best, when TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url) is nil it always enqueues Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...) and renders the loading template. app/views/embed/loading.html.erb contains a setTimeout that unconditionally reloads the page every 30 seconds with no cap/backoff. If retrieval never succeeds (e.g., remote fetch keeps failing or invalid content), the iframe will keep re-requesting /embed/best and each request will enqueue another RetrieveTopic job, creating an unbounded loop of reloads and job enqueues (the TopicRetriever throttle only prevents the fetch from running more than once per 60s; it does not stop the controller from enqueuing jobs repeatedly).

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:41-46 — spec asserts `TopicRetriever.expects(:new)` while the controller enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)`, so it does not verify the job is enqueued with the right embed_url/user_id

adjudication.rationale: In `app/controllers/embed_controller.rb#best`, when `topic_id` is nil it does **not** instantiate `TopicRetriever`; it calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, user_id: current_user.try(:id), embed_url: embed_url)` and renders `loading`. However `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb` asserts `TopicRetriever.expects(:new)` and `retriever.expects(:retrieve)` in the "no previous embed" case, which doesn’t match the controller behavior and also fails to assert the job enqueue arguments (`embed_url`/`user_id`). This is a concrete mismatch introduced in the diff and would make the spec incorrect/failing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:18-28 — the 'requires feed_polling_url' and 'requires embed_by_username' examples never stub `feed_polling_enabled?` to true, so they pass even if the URL/username guards were deleted

adjudication.rationale: In Jobs::PollFeed#execute, poll_feed is only called if all three conditions are true: feed_polling_enabled?, feed_polling_url.present?, and embed_by_username.present?. In spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb the “requires feed_polling_url” and “requires embed_by_username” examples only stub the URL/username to nil and never stub feed_polling_enabled? to true. Given the default in config/site_settings.yml is feed_polling_enabled: false, these specs will (and can) pass because the first guard fails, meaning they do not actually verify that the URL/username guards exist; removing those guards would not necessarily break these tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:56-58 — `absolutize_urls` only rewrites hrefs/srcs beginning with `/`, leaving document-relative (`images/foo.jpg`, `../x`) and protocol-relative (`//host/x`) URLs unhandled

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls`, both the `` and `` rewrites only run when the URL `start_with?('/')` (see the `if href.present? && href.start_with?('/')` / `if src.present? && src.start_with?('/')` conditions). That means document-relative paths like `images/foo.jpg` or `../x` are left unchanged, and protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.example.com/x` are also not handled. Given the method’s stated purpose (“Convert any relative URLs to absolute”), leaving these common relative forms unconverted can cause broken links/images when the HTML is rendered from the Discourse domain instead of the source site.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:53 — port suffix logic compares against both 80 and 443 regardless of scheme, so `http://host:443/...` and `https://host:80/...` lose their port and produce wrong absolute URLs

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls, the prefix is built as "#{uri.scheme}://#{uri.host}" and then it appends ":#{uri.port}" only if uri.port != 80 && uri.port != 443. This treats both 80 and 443 as “default” ports regardless of scheme. For example, with url "http://example.com:443/path", uri.scheme is "http" and uri.port is 443, so the condition is false and the code omits :443, producing "http://example.com" instead of "http://example.com:443". Similarly, "https://example.com:80" would incorrectly omit :80. That yields wrong absolute URLs for relative links/images in those (unusual but valid) cases.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:5-11 — no null check on `document.getElementById('discourse-comments')`, so `comments.appendChild` throws and breaks the host page's JS when the container is missing or not yet parsed

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js`, `comments` is set via `document.getElementById('discourse-comments')` and then immediately used as `comments.appendChild(iframe)` with no guard. If the host page does not include an element with that id, or if this script runs before that element exists in the DOM, `comments` will be `null` and `appendChild` will throw a TypeError, potentially breaking further JS execution on the host page. This is directly verifiable from lines 5–11 of the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Gemfile:209-210 — `ruby-readability` and `simple-rss` added to the Gemfile with only Gemfile_rails4.lock regenerated; the Rails 3 `Gemfile.lock` is out of date and `bundle install --deployment` will fail on that path

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `ruby-readability` and `simple-rss` to `Gemfile` and updates only `Gemfile_rails4.lock`. However, there is no `Gemfile.lock` (Rails 3 lockfile) shown in the diff, so we cannot verify from this change alone that a Rails 3 lockfile exists, is required in this repo, or is now out of date. The claim that `bundle install --deployment` will fail on a Rails 3 path is therefore not directly verifiable from the provided diff.
